after: ## Where this fits in the subject
alt: Four rows: A knowing and understanding (apply knowledge to unfamiliar contexts), B inquiring and designing (own testable question, variables and justified method), C processing and evaluating (accurate data work, specific limitation and improvement) and D reflecting on the impacts of science (two-sided, cited, reasoned judgement). The descriptors are the same for every course model.
caption: Each criterion rewards using a skill, not naming it, and none changes with the course model.

alt: A hand on a metal spoon loses heat quickly, shown by thick arrows, so the spoon feels colder; a hand on a wooden spoon loses heat slowly, so it feels warmer. Both spoons are actually at room temperature. A lower-band answer only names thermal conductivity; a top-band answer uses conduction rate to judge actual versus perceived temperature.
caption: Top-band criterion A answers use the concept to reach and justify a judgement.

alt: Lower band follows a fixed worksheet on temperature and reaction rate. Top band has the student write a research question on how reactant concentration affects reaction rate, a testable hypothesis, the independent variable (concentration), dependent variable (rate) and controlled variables with reasons, and a justified method.
caption: Top-band criterion B work is the student’s own question, variables and justified method.

alt: A graph with labelled axes plots reaction rate against reactant concentration with a line of best fit. The steps are identify the trend, explain it with a concept such as collision theory, and evaluate the method. “Use more trials” is generic; top band names the real limitation, an endpoint judged by eye, and a matching fix, a colorimeter.
caption: Name a real weakness of your own method and a fix that targets exactly that weakness.

after: ## Criterion D: Reflecting on the impacts of science
alt: A balance weighs a genuine benefit of genetically modified crops, increased yield in specific conditions, against a genuine risk, ecological or economic concerns, each with a cited source. Above it, the answer weighs both and reaches a reasoned judgement. A one-sided or purely descriptive answer cannot reach the top band.
caption: A top-band criterion D answer is two-sided, sourced and ends in a judgement.

after: ## Why the four criteria are usually assessed through one connected investigation
alt: A single practical investigation in the centre sends evidence to all four criteria: A, the scientific concept behind it; B, its design; C, processing and evaluating the data; and, where relevant, D, its wider scientific or real-world significance.
caption: One well-designed investigation usually produces evidence for all four criteria.
